asl.hook: Think of working with a hammer: one fist pounds on the other.
steps: Make fists (the S handshape) with both hands.
Turn both palms to face down.
Hold your non-dominant fist still in front of you.
Tap the wrist or side of it with your dominant fist a few times.
asl.tip: Many signers use a handshape between an A and an S, especially on the dominant hand; that is fine. For a job, the sign JOB is more common.

fact.text: The Antarctic Ice Sheet covers almost 14 million square kilometers, roughly the area of the contiguous United States and Mexico combined, and is nearly 4.9 kilometers thick at its deepest point. If all of it melted, global sea level would rise by about 58 meters.

onThisDay.text: Jean-Francois Pilatre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes made the first free flight carrying people, in a hot-air balloon built by the Montgolfier brothers. They lifted off from the garden of the Chateau de la Muette in Paris in front of the king, rose to about 3,000 feet and drifted about 9 kilometers in some 25 minutes before landing at the Butte-aux-Cailles. Two months earlier, a sheep, a duck and a rooster had made a test flight at Versailles.
onThisDay.title: First Balloon Flight

lead.headline: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% as AI sell-off pushes market into correction
more: Nvidia fell 13.8%, and is down more than 25% since the scandal that led co-founder Jensen Huang to resign as chief executive on Nov. 12. AMD lost 13.3%, Micron 13.9% and Broadcom 12.1%; the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 10.7%. Anthropic shares dropped 9.1% to $88.30, still above their $83 IPO price.
The S&P 500 posted its worst week since April 2025. Its seven-day losing streak was the longest since early 2020. Most stocks outside tech rose. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.91%.

CBS News also pointed to proposed limits on data center construction expected after the midterm elections, and to a Dec. 11 government funding deadline. A Baird strategist said the idea that AI spending can keep propping up the market is ending, but that he does not think the bull market that began in October 2022 is over.
lead.summary: U.S. stocks suffered one of their worst days in years on Friday as a sell-off in artificial intelligence and chip stocks deepened. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39, putting it more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record and in a correction, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3% and turned negative for the year. The Dow lost 949.73 points, or 1.9%. Investors are questioning whether heavy AI spending will pay off, amid fallout from the Nvidia leadership scandal, tighter chip export rules, expected Fed rate increases and tensions with Iran.

briefs.text: Young Socialists (Jusos) planned protests on Friday in Zurich, Basel, Bern, Lausanne and other cities as part of a Europe-wide movement against militarization and austerity; organizers said no riots were planned.
The French-speaking cantons and Ticino want to strengthen German teaching from primary school onward, calling skills in a national language essential for national cohesion.

stories.headline: Parts of Swiss Alps put on high avalanche alert
more: The level 4 zones include Bex-Villars, the Wildhorn area, western and northern Lower Valais and the Martigny-Verbier area, where the main risk is avalanches set off by the weight of the snow itself, possibly reaching lower elevations. Parts of eastern Switzerland are at level 3, where a single person on a steep slope can trigger a slide.

Up to 50 centimeters of fresh snow could fall on northern slopes above 1,800 meters, and the Bernese Oberland could get up to 30 centimeters more by Sunday along with gale-force winds. About 20 people die in avalanches in Switzerland in an average year.
stories.summary: The Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research (SLF) raised the avalanche danger to level 4, the second-highest on its scale, for parts of Vaud, Valais and Bern on Friday. Heavy snowfall is forecast to continue through Sunday.

stories.headline: Left launches initiative to cut health insurance premiums
more: Backers say 90 percent of the population would benefit. They must now collect enough signatures to force a nationwide vote.
stories.summary: The Social Democrats, the Greens and trade unions announced a popular initiative on Thursday that would make insurers waive two months of premiums a year for each adult and six months for each child. The plan would cost about 8 billion francs a year, funded by a higher direct federal tax on individual income and business profits.

stories.headline: Zurich University Hospital pays first compensation in heart surgery scandal
more: The hospital says all cases so far were settled out of court and several claims are still pending. A report in May found 68 to 74 more deaths than statistically expected among about 4,500 heart operations under former department head Francesco Maisano.
Zurich prosecutors are investigating three cases on suspicion of negligent homicide, negligent serious bodily harm and document forgery.
stories.summary: The University Hospital of Zurich (USZ) has paid compensation in 14 cases to patients or surviving relatives affected by failings in its cardiac surgery department. It has received 20 claims in total, and the payments so far add up to a low six-figure sum in francs.

briefs.text: Leaked Deutsche Bank documents point to a suspected Russian money-laundering network that moved at least 1.7 billion euros through Hungary's MKB bank between 2017 and 2020, according to Hungarian outlet Direkt36; Deutsche Bank ended its relationship with MKB.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves overhaul of custody and child support rules
more: The Justice Ministry calls the custody bill the biggest reform of child law since 1998. It defines domestic violence to include physical, sexual, psychological and economic abuse and would let the parent caring for a child make routine decisions alone. It is expected to take effect in the second half of 2027 at the earliest.

From 2029, single parents with taxable income above 40,000 euros a year, plus 10,000 euros for each additional child, would lose entitlement to advance maintenance. Parents who owe support and refuse to disclose their finances could face fines or a driving ban. Both bills still need Bundestag approval.
stories.summary: The federal cabinet approved two draft bills that would let courts bar contact with a parent who is violent toward the other parent and give teenagers aged 14 and over a greater say in custody arrangements. A second bill would tighten state advance maintenance payments for single parents.

stories.headline: Conservatives make new push to tighten citizenship rules
more: The proposal from Guenter Krings and Alexander Throm would reverse much of the 2024 reform. The coalition partner SPD has so far blocked such changes, but Bild reported that its leadership is reviewing the proposal, which may be offered in exchange for stronger residency rights for foreigners in work or training. Party leaders are expected to discuss it next week.
stories.summary: CDU/CSU lawmakers proposed raising the residency requirement for naturalization back to eight years from five, allowing dual citizenship only in exceptional cases and requiring B2-level German. The plan would also bar applicants who receive social assistance.

stories.headline: Electricity tax cut for all households to return in 2027
more: Funding is secured only through the end of 2027 from the renewable-energy surcharge account; the coalition says it intends the cut to be permanent but must find financing in the 2028 budget. Comparison site Verivox estimates a three-person household using 4,000 kilowatt-hours would save about 7.75 euros a month. The Bundestag is due to vote on the 2027 budget on November 27.
stories.summary: Coalition leaders agreed after more than eight hours of budget talks to cut the electricity tax for all households and businesses from 2.05 cents to 0.1 cents per kilowatt-hour, the EU minimum, starting January 1. The cut will cost about 5.4 billion euros a year.

briefs.text: Native oysters have bred naturally in Scotland's Dornoch Firth for the first time in more than a century, Heriot-Watt University said, after a restoration project that has released over 140,000 juvenile oysters since 2017 found young spat growing on the seabed.

Britain's Judicial Committee of the Privy Council ruled unanimously on November 10 that Trinidad and Tobago's laws criminalizing consensual sex between adults of the same sex are unconstitutional, in a case brought by activist Jason Jones.

stories.headline: Eritrea eliminates trachoma as a public health problem
more: Eritrea surveyed all 58 of its sub-zobas between 2006 and 2020 and applied WHO's SAFE strategy of eyelid surgery, antibiotics, facial cleanliness and better water and sanitation, using azithromycin donated by Pfizer through the International Trachoma Initiative. It is the 66th country to eliminate at least one neglected tropical disease.

Worldwide, the number of people needing trachoma interventions fell from about 1.5 billion in 2002 to below 100 million by November 2025, a drop of about 94 percent. WHO says 92 million people still lived in endemic areas as of March 2026, and the disease remains a public health problem in parts of 29 countries.
stories.summary: The World Health Organization said on November 16 that it has validated Eritrea's elimination of trachoma, the world's leading infectious cause of blindness, as a public health problem. Eritrea is the 34th country worldwide and the 11th in WHO's African Region to reach the milestone. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said two decades of effort had consigned the disease to history in the country.

briefs.text: Finance Minister Elisabeth Svantesson costed the Social Democrats' policy offers to the Centre Party at 175 billion kronor; Centre leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist said the package would be unsustainable in full and must be negotiated.
Six pupils at the Sigtunaskolan Humanistiska Laroverket boarding school were charged with bullying and assaulting younger students, two of them with serious sexual assault; all deny wrongdoing.
Forsmark 1 and 3 nuclear reactors were due back online after maintenance and a cable fault, easing power supply; Vattenfall said Ringhals 3 and 4 will not restart until early December.
More than nine in ten women feel safe with Swedish maternity care, a survey by the association of local authorities and regions found, though many report too little follow-up after birth.

stories.headline: Snow warning issued for Stockholm and Uppsala
more: The warning covers an area from Nynashamn and Sodertalje in the south to Tierp in the north. Along the northern Uppland coast most of the precipitation is expected to fall as rain.
stories.summary: The weather agency SMHI issued a yellow warning for 5 to 15 centimeters of fresh snow in the Stockholm and Uppsala area from Friday evening to Saturday evening. It warned of longer travel times and possible public transport delays and cancellations.

stories.headline: Trial opens for teenager accused of planning IS-inspired school attack
more: He was arrested at 18, the day after the Easter holidays. Prosecutors say he planned to use a kitchen knife; his defense lawyer argues the risk he would have carried out an attack was small and that he had no real links to IS.
stories.summary: A 19-year-old went on trial charged with preparing a terrorist offense after prosecutors said he planned to kill 15 people at his upper secondary school in Halmstad. He denies the charge, saying he changed his mind at the last minute, but admits taking part in a terrorist organization and publicly inciting terrorism.

briefs.text: The Senate voted 62-33 on Thursday for a bipartisan bill to speed up approvals for power plants and transmission lines. The bill would also make large AI data centers pay more toward grid upgrades. It now goes to the House.
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan to close Rikers Island by 2032, five years later than the previous deadline. Four smaller borough jails would replace it.

A federal appeals court blocked the Army from detonating several tons of unstable bomb-making chemicals in Iowa over health concerns. Separately, a second federal judge halted construction of Trump's planned memorial arch near Arlington National Cemetery.
Trump said Nvidia should give Jensen Huang a second chance, but Nvidia's board chair said directors do not plan to reinstate him.

stories.headline: U.S. and Israel weigh new strikes on Iran, sources say
more: Sources said an offensive could begin within two to four days if ordered. The U.S. has tens of thousands of troops and two carrier strike groups in the region.

Indirect talks have not produced a ceasefire to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and tit-for-tat strikes continue nine months into the war. Iran's Foreign Ministry compared U.S. allegations about Iranian weapons to the case made before the 2003 invasion of Iraq.
stories.summary: Israel and the United States are considering a new military assault on Iran in the near term, CBS News reported, citing unnamed sources. Israel is concerned that Iran is rebuilding ballistic missile production and moving sites underground. President Trump said he was not rushing into any decision.

stories.headline: Man convicted of starting deadly Palisades Fire
more: Prosecutors said a fire he started on Jan. 1, 2025, smoldered underground and flared up on Jan. 7, becoming one of the most destructive wildfires in California history. They relied on cellphone data, camera images and his texts.
The defense argued the scene had been open to the public for days and that fireworks may have caused the fire.
stories.summary: A federal jury in a retrial on Friday convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, of arson and destroying property by fire in connection with the January 2025 Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people. The first trial ended in a mistrial in June.

stories.headline: String of U.S. outages raises cybersecurity concerns
more: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the outages likely came from organizations using AI to fix security flaws and run maintenance updates. Experts quoted by Al Jazeera said the administration is not taking AI-driven threats seriously, noting that the cybersecurity agency CISA lost more than a third of its staff in 2025 cuts.
stories.summary: A series of recent outages hit major banks, Microsoft, Apple and Workday, along with a national aviation ground stop and an NSA internal network. President Trump told the public to relax, calling them individual events, and the White House fired the U.S. cybersecurity chief on Thursday.

briefs.text: Denmark is expelling Russia's defense attache after its intelligence service said Russian agents planned to kill a Ukrainian rapper at a Copenhagen-area concert in September. Russia's embassy said Denmark had shown no evidence.
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh after it struck Hodeidah port and Sanaa. The Houthis have threatened Saudi ports and power plants.
The European-Japanese spacecraft BepiColombo is about to go into orbit around Mercury, eight years after launch. It will be only the second spacecraft to orbit the planet.

stories.headline: Poland calls Russian missiles in its territory an intentional provocation
more: Possible impact sites were reported near Nowy Lipowiec, about 60 km from the Ukrainian border, and around Bilgoraj County. No casualties were reported. Poland said it would ask NATO for more help securing the alliance's eastern flank, and Rutte was due in Warsaw on Saturday.
Tusk said Poland must have a say in decisions about Ukraine's future. Russian strikes on Ukraine overnight included an attack on a railway station in the west of the country.
stories.summary: Poland said two missiles and a drone that came down in its eastern regions overnight were probably Russian. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an intentional provocation by Moscow. The objects came down during a military exercise involving the Coalition of the Willing, a group of European countries preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called the incident clearly dangerous.

stories.headline: COP31 climate talks go into overtime over fossil fuels
more: The European Union warned the summit risked becoming a fossil summit, and Panama threatened to walk out. The new text also dropped a $120 billion target for helping poorer countries adapt.
A third draft was expected Saturday. COP31 president Murat Kurum said negotiators were close to the finish line but not there yet. The United States is absent for a second year.
stories.summary: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkiye, ran past its Friday deadline without a deal. Nearly 200 countries remain split over fossil fuels. A revised draft dropped all mention of them after objections from Saudi Arabia and other oil and gas producers.

stories.headline: UK and EU agree closer trade, carbon and youth mobility ties
more: No documents were signed, and each side still has to complete legal procedures. Tuition fees for EU students and British access to EU 'Made in Europe' rules remain unresolved.
stories.summary: At a summit in Brussels on Friday, Britain and the European Union agreed to ease food and farm checks, link their carbon trading systems, and let up to 100,000 young people from each side live and work in the other's territory. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the package could add 0.5% to UK economic output.

stories.headline: Estonia to close road border with Russia from December
more: Estonia's foreign minister said the closure would limit recruitment, sabotage and sanctions evasion. Rail freight will continue under strict checks. Finland has kept its Russian crossings closed since 2023.
stories.summary: Estonia's government approved a six-month closure of all road crossings with Russia starting Dec. 1. It accused Moscow of an attempted arson attack on a drone maker, which the Kremlin denies. Russia's Foreign Ministry said the move amounted to a new Iron Curtain and promised a response.

asl.hook: Home is where you eat and sleep: you start near the mouth (eat) and move toward the ear, where your head rests (sleep).
steps: Bring the fingertips and thumb of your dominant hand together.
Touch them to your cheek near the side of your mouth.
Move the hand an inch or two back toward your ear.
Touch your cheek again.
asl.tip: The sign is made on the cheek, not on the mouth itself. Some signers move from ear to mouth instead; both are fine.

fact.text: Sea otters have the densest fur of any animal, with roughly 500,000 to one million hairs per square inch of skin. By comparison, a person has about 100,000 hairs on their whole head. Unlike seals, sea otters have no blubber layer and stay warm in cold ocean water thanks to that fur and a fast metabolism.

lead.headline: World Court finds Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
more: The Gambia urged Myanmar to comply fully and without delay, and Bangladesh said safe repatriation remains the only workable solution to the crisis. Myanmar's shadow National Unity Government said it respects the court's authority.

The UN refugee agency says more than 1.3 million Rohingya refugees remain displaced across the region, most of them in Bangladesh, and more than 100,000 people are internally displaced in Rakhine State.
lead.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled in The Hague on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the mostly Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017, the first time the court has held a state responsible for genocide. The case was brought by the Gambia in 2019 under the 1948 Genocide Convention, with backing from the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation. The court ordered Myanmar to compensate the Rohingya, with the amount and terms to be set later. Britain responded by expelling Myanmar's defense attache and calling for an urgent UN Security Council session.

briefs.text: A Council of Europe report says Switzerland has made significant progress in protecting linguistic diversity and national minorities, with the revised Languages Act boosting Italian and Romansh.

stories.headline: Switzerland to require original ID documents from foreign residents
more: Authorities would have to verify originals systematically at a foreigner's first contact, confirm they are authentic and check that they belong to the person presenting them. The justice ministry has been tasked with drafting the proposal.

A consultation runs until March 5, 2027, after which the government and parliament will decide how and when to implement the change. A 2025 investigation by broadcaster SRF found thousands of foreigners living in Switzerland illegally on counterfeit European passports.
stories.summary: The Federal Council decided on Wednesday to tighten rules so that foreign nationals registering with cantonal and municipal authorities must present original identity documents rather than copies. The government says current checks are not thorough enough and have enabled fraud in a number of cases.

stories.headline: Swiss who fought in WWII resistance to be rehabilitated
more: Serving in a foreign army is a punishable offense in Switzerland, and the wartime government convicted citizens who joined the French and Italian resistance. The government says it will now recognize their actions as a fight for democracy and freedom.
stories.summary: The Federal Council announced a law taking effect on January 1, 2027, that rehabilitates Swiss citizens convicted for joining foreign resistance movements against Nazi Germany and fascism. In most cases the rehabilitation will be posthumous.

stories.headline: Switzerland ranks 27th in global English proficiency index
more: Switzerland scored 557 points. The study found Swiss adults particularly weak at speaking and writing English at a high level.
stories.summary: Switzerland placed 27th worldwide and 20th in Europe in language school EF's 2026 English Proficiency Index, well behind neighbors Germany and Austria. The ranking is based on free online tests taken by about 2.3 million adults in 117 countries in 2025.

briefs.text: The Federal Constitutional Court rejected the BSW party's bid for a recount of the February 2025 election, in which it narrowly missed the 5 percent threshold; the result stands.
Three researchers working on light-based data transfer for optical microchips, led by Christian Koos of the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, won the 250,000 euro German Future Prize.
Germany and Austria are pushing for control of TikTok's operations in Europe.

stories.headline: Berlin hosts Coalition of the Willing summit on Ukraine
more: Ukraine faces a funding gap of about 70 billion euros next year, and the EU has proposed an additional 45 billion euro loan. Britain was expected to announce more than 1,000 long-range strike drones.
The summit followed a planned meeting in Shenzhen, China, between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. A Kremlin aide called the Shenzhen talks the main event and Berlin secondary.
stories.summary: Germany, France and Britain co-hosted a summit of Ukraine's allies in Berlin on Thursday, expected to bring together more than 30 European leaders, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. The meeting aimed to give Europe a bigger role in efforts to end the nearly five-year war.

stories.headline: Berlin faces at least 2 billion euros in civil servant back pay
more: The payments follow a Federal Constitutional Court ruling that Berlin underpaid civil servants between 2008 and 2020. Only staff who filed lawsuits are entitled to back pay; paying everyone would cost about 7 billion euros for 2008 to 2020 alone.
Officials expect further costs of about 180 million euros a year. The city must decide who qualifies by the end of March 2027.
stories.summary: Berlin must pay its civil servants at least 2 billion euros in back pay for 2008 to 2025, the city's finance department confirmed to broadcaster rbb. That is well above an earlier estimate of 1.2 billion euros from Finance Senator Stefan Evers.

stories.headline: GLS and DPD to merge German parcel operations
more: The venture expects to handle about 700 million parcels a year with revenue above 4 billion euros, employ around 15,000 people and invest more than 500 million euros, mainly in IT and automated pickup stations. The DPD brand will disappear.
Market leader DHL handled about two billion German parcels last year.
stories.summary: Parcel carriers GLS and DPD plan to combine their German operations in a joint venture, with GLS's owner holding 80 percent and DPD's French parent Geopost 20 percent. The deal still needs regulatory approval.

briefs.text: The 2026 Earthshot Prize went to Ørsted, PFAS-Free France, Bhutan, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Niue Ocean Wide Trust, each receiving 1 million pounds; Bhutan became the first country to win, for a plan to restore 50,000 hectares of damaged land.

A mountain guide found a high-altitude cave in South Tyrol's Fanes-Senes-Braies Natural Park holding hundreds of bones believed to belong to extinct cave bears; authorities have gated the entrance while researchers prepare to study the remains.

stories.headline: Voyager 1 becomes the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth
more: Voyager 1 travels at about 38,000 mph. Both Voyager probes lose about 4 watts of power a year, and engineers switched off three devices earlier this year in favor of lower-power alternatives, a step NASA expects to keep the current science instruments running until at least the 50th launch anniversaries next summer.
NASA said the team has not received science or engineering data from Voyager 1 since Nov. 14, though the probe is still sending a carrier signal, and engineers are analyzing the problem.
stories.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth at 2:16 a.m. PST on Nov. 18, meaning a radio signal now takes a full day to travel between the probe and Earth. The distance is about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers), the farthest any human-made object has gone. The spacecraft launched in 1977 and has been in interstellar space since 2012.

briefs.text: The Church of Sweden's General Synod rejected a motion to end priests' right to refuse to marry same-sex couples and ordered a further report, due by 2028.
Sweden Democrat MP Rasmus Giertz, who faces misconduct allegations he denies, now says he will keep his seat; the party has suspended his membership pending an internal investigation.
Rail operator SJ will relaunch a night train from Sweden to Berlin via Copenhagen in December.
Sweden ranked first in the world in EF's 2026 English Proficiency Index.

stories.headline: Speaker sets Christmas deadline for new Swedish government
more: Moderate leader Ulf Kristersson, who has explored a centre-right government with the Christian Democrats, Liberals and Centre Party, told the speaker the Centre Party needs more time to decide.

The Social Democrats have offered the Centre Party a 135-point package for a government with the Greens, cooperating with the Left Party. The Greens called it a good starting point but said four-party talks had not begun.
stories.summary: Parliamentary Speaker Andreas Norlén said Sweden should know by Christmas whether it will have a new government or a snap election, and gave party leaders one more week of talks. He plans to call them back to parliament next week, with a possible vote at the end of November.

stories.headline: Moderates overtake Social Democrats in poll for first time since 2016
more: The poll comes two months after the September election, with no government formed yet. Novus chairman Torbjorn Sjostrom said the Social Democrats have lost support in two consecutive polls.
stories.summary: A Novus poll for TV4 put the Moderate Party at 26.5 percent and the Social Democrats at 24.9 percent, the first Novus survey since May 2016 with the Moderates ahead. The parties of the former governing Tido bloc lead the red-green parties by 6.3 points.

briefs.text: A federal appeals court let the administration proceed for now with ending deportation protections for about 600,000 Venezuelans under Temporary Protected Status, while legal challenges continue.
President Trump said he posthumously pardoned baseball's all-time hits leader Pete Rose, who served five months in prison for federal tax crimes in 1990.
The FCC voted to allow state prisons to jam signals from contraband cellphones.

stories.headline: Record rain floods South Florida, closing schools
more: Florida's governor declared a state of emergency for affected areas, a hospital temporarily suspended visits after a breach, and the roof of a synagogue in Hollywood collapsed.
The National Weather Service kept flood watches in effect through Thursday night for Miami, Fort Lauderdale and Palm Beach, with more rain forecast.
stories.summary: Parts of Broward County received more than 15 inches of rain since Tuesday, flooding streets, homes and classrooms in Hollywood, Davie and Fort Lauderdale. The county declared a state of emergency and closed schools, and wildlife officers rescued more than 70 residents from a flooded apartment complex in Hollywood. No injuries or deaths have been reported.

stories.headline: Senate rejects another Iran war powers resolution
more: The war with Iran began in late February. Democrats have forced more than a dozen war powers votes since then; the Senate passed a similar measure in June with four Republican votes.
The resolution's effect would have been largely symbolic: administrations of both parties have argued such concurrent resolutions are unconstitutional.
stories.summary: The Senate voted 48-51 on Thursday against a House-passed resolution directing the president to remove US forces from hostilities with Iran. Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul voted in favor, while Democrat John Fetterman joined most Republicans in opposition.

stories.headline: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq after largest IPO on record
more: The debut came on a rough day for Wall Street: the Dow fell more than 1,100 points, the Nasdaq dropped more than 2 percent, and the S&P 500 fell for a sixth straight day amid concerns about AI, PBS NewsHour reported.
stories.summary: AI company Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday after pricing its shares at $83, above an earlier range of $70 to $78. The offering of 980 million shares raised $81.3 billion, the largest IPO in history, and valued the company at about $1.5 trillion.

briefs.text: Saudi authorities said a tower in Riyadh was hit in a Houthi attack, Al Jazeera reported in its coverage of the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The European Commission confirmed it was the target of an AI-generated cyberattack in October; the perpetrator is unknown and the investigation is ongoing.

stories.headline: Putin rules out limited ceasefire after strikes on Crimea bridge
more: Putin spoke to reporters after his meeting with President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Russian state media said rail traffic on the bridge was briefly halted after a third Ukrainian strike in four days.
Ukraine's allies met in Berlin, where President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine must take part in any future talks and suggested a four-way meeting including Russia.
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow will not agree to a limited ceasefire with Ukraine after Ukrainian missile strikes damaged the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, and he vowed a severe response. A Russian drone later damaged the Dutch embassy and a cathedral in Kyiv, killing at least one person, according to a Ukrainian official.

stories.headline: Bukele set to register bid for third straight term
more: Rights groups say his years-long state of emergency against gangs has brought mass arrests and detentions without charge and mass trials. Bukele is widely seen as the clear favorite.
stories.summary: El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele is expected to formally register as a candidate for a third consecutive term in the February 28, 2027, election, with Vice President Felix Ulloa as his running mate. A 2025 constitutional amendment passed by his party's legislative majority allowed a third term and extended terms to six years.

fact.text: A honeybee's waggle dance tells its nestmates the direction of a food source and how far the dancer thinks it flew, judged by how much scenery streamed past its eyes rather than by true distance. lead.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first three-way summit in Shenzhen
more: Putin met Xi on Wednesday. Beijing has said the three-way meeting will have groundbreaking significance, and Trump has said he wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals. The Pentagon projects China will have more than 1,000 nuclear warheads by 2030, still far fewer than the U.S. and Russia.

Trade tensions remain: Washington recently tightened curbs meant to keep high-end chips from reaching China, and Beijing answered with export limits on rare earth magnets used in electric vehicles and fighter jets.

Trump and Putin last met in Alaska in August 2025 without a Ukraine settlement. U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected in Berlin on Thursday to meet Ukrainian and European officials on post-war security guarantees and a recovery plan; a U.S. official called the Berlin and China meetings a coordinated diplomatic effort.
lead.summary: President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin are set to meet together on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, the first formal meeting of the leaders of the three powers. Trump arrived in southern China on Wednesday after a stop in the Philippines, and Xi greeted him personally at the airport. Trump is also scheduled to hold his third bilateral meeting of the year with Xi and a one-on-one with Putin, according to a U.S. official. There is no official agenda, but Ukraine, Iran, trade and nuclear weapons are expected to come up.

stories.headline: Poll shows pension funding plan narrowly trailing ahead of Nov. 29 vote
more: According to the second SBC poll, 51 percent of voters in Switzerland oppose a 0.4 percentage point VAT increase to fund the 13th pension payment, while 56 percent of Swiss abroad back it.

The "Fair Taxation Initiative," which would end the tax penalty on married couples, has only 40 percent approval. A reform easing arms export rules is too close to call, with 49 percent in favor, 46 percent against and 5 percent undecided.
An initiative to restrict the sale and use of noisy fireworks has 63 percent support. The national votes take place on Nov. 29.
stories.summary: A new poll for the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation shows a narrow majority of voters opposed to raising value-added tax to pay for the 13th monthly old-age pension. A plan to end the tax penalty on married couples looks set to fail, while a fireworks initiative has strong support.

stories.headline: Switzerland weighs joining five-nation Rwanda deportation center
more: The five countries said the center, due to open in 2027 as a pilot, would take around 100 people whose asylum claims were rejected and who refuse to return home. Minors would be excluded.

A Swiss justice ministry spokesperson said Switzerland would examine participating if the project proves "fruitful, sustainable and feasible." The Senate broadly backed a motion along those lines by Petra Gossi last summer; Social Democrat Jean Tschopp opposes the idea.
stories.summary: Switzerland will consider taking part in a planned center in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers if the project proves workable, a justice ministry spokesperson said. Germany, Austria, Denmark, the Netherlands and Greece announced the plan this week.

stories.headline: Initiative launched to keep Swiss e-ID voluntary in the constitution
more: The initiative, "Digital yes, but freely chosen," is backed by organizers linked to Nova, an association founded a month earlier. They need 100,000 signatures by May 17, 2028.

The e-ID is expected to roll out in the first half of 2027. The government says there is no general obligation to obtain or use one, though individual services could become digital-only if specific legislation requires it.
stories.summary: Opponents of compulsory digital identification launched a popular initiative on Tuesday to write the voluntary use of the planned Swiss e-ID into the constitution. The government says the e-ID will remain voluntary.

briefs.text: The Bundestag voted 308 to 190, with 71 abstentions, to let the BND and domestic intelligence actively disrupt threats such as hostile servers, with most provisions due to take effect Dec. 31.
Online check-in for Lufthansa Group flights, including Swiss, now requires a free Travel ID account, with the rule in force at Munich and Zurich since Nov. 16 and at Frankfurt from Nov. 30.

stories.headline: Germany and four EU partners plan deportation center in Rwanda
more: The center would take around 100 people whose asylum claims were rejected after all appeals and who refuse to return to their home countries. People of any nationality would be eligible; minors are excluded.

The five governments say the center would be open, without detention, and that stays of a few months would include vocational training and language courses. The site has been chosen but not disclosed, and officials have not said what Rwanda would receive.
The countries cite recent EU returns legislation as the legal basis. NGOs have raised concerns about the treatment of migrants, and court challenges are expected.
stories.summary: Germany, Austria, Denmark, the Netherlands and Greece announced plans for a center in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers, the first such facility outside the EU. A pilot is planned for next year.

stories.headline: Berlin bans Neukolln mosque association over Hezbollah support
more: More than 50 officers took part in the operation centered on the association's community center on Flughafenstrasse in Neukolln. Authorities said the group supported Hezbollah organizationally and financially and used its youth work and its Markaz Al Qaem mosque to spread propaganda.

Interior Senator Iris Spranger said the association's purpose and activities run contrary to criminal law. The ban is an administrative decision that the association can challenge in court. Hezbollah activity has been banned in Germany since 2020.
stories.summary: Berlin's interior department banned the mosque association El-Irschad and three affiliated groups on Tuesday, saying they supported Hezbollah. Police searched 28 premises.

stories.headline: EU clears UniCredit takeover of Commerzbank
more: The European Central Bank had already approved the deal. The Commission said UniCredit, which owns HypoVereinsbank, and Commerzbank would together hold a moderate share of German banking services.

Berlin initially opposed the takeover but shifted this year, with Chancellor Friedrich Merz saying the government would not block it. Commerzbank chief Bettina Orlopp said the decision was no surprise and that nothing changes for clients for now.
stories.summary: The European Commission approved Italian bank UniCredit's hostile takeover of Commerzbank, finding no competition concerns. UniCredit has built a stake of nearly 50 percent.

briefs.text: Kenya launched a 10-year, 160 million dollar conservation program, half funded by the government, covering 17.3 million hectares across 31 counties and projected to benefit about 1.6 million people.
NYU Abu Dhabi researchers found that Endozoicomonas bacteria in corals from the hot Arabian Gulf produce steroid hormones linked to heat resistance, pointing toward possible coral probiotics.

Revolution Wind, a 704-megawatt farm off Rhode Island and Connecticut, became the third U.S. utility-scale offshore wind project in full operation, enough for more than 350,000 New England homes, according to Orsted.

stories.headline: Ethiopian water mouse found alive nearly a century after last record
more: Ecologist Mengistu Wale of the Ethiopian Biodiversity Institute found the first one in a trap baited with peanut butter during a biodiversity survey; the team later caught two more. Genetic tests to confirm the identification are underway.

The amphibious rodent, Nilopegamys plumbeus, has dense fur, large hind feet and extensive whiskers that may help it find aquatic insects. Its original habitat in northern Ethiopia was largely converted to farmland, and it remains listed as critically endangered.
stories.summary: Scientists have captured three Ethiopian water mice, a species known from a single specimen collected in 1927 and presumed extinct. The animals turned up in a stream in the Yayu Coffee Forest Biosphere Reserve in southwestern Ethiopia.

briefs.text: Electricity retailer Bixia forecasts winter prices averaging about 1.50 kronor per kilowatt-hour in the Stockholm zone and about 1.80 in southern Sweden, slightly above the 2022-23 crisis winter on average.
The Church of Sweden's General Synod rejected ending priests' right to refuse to marry same-sex couples and ordered a report on its view of marriage by 2028.

Parliament approved a constitutional amendment 292 to 51 that allows revoking citizenship from dual nationals who obtained it fraudulently or are convicted of crimes seriously harming Sweden's vital interests, effective Jan. 1.
Sweden Democrat MP Rasmus Giertz reversed plans to resign after a newspaper investigation into his behavior toward women, which he denies; his party has suspended his membership pending an inquiry.

stories.headline: Swedish parties restore pairing deal after citizenship vote breakdown
more: The earlier system broke down on April 29 when the Sweden Democrats brought in two members they had agreed to hold back, to defeat transitional citizenship rules that would have let about 100,000 applicants be judged under older rules.

Under the new deal, 36 of 349 members can be excused in each session. If it is breached, parties must consult and work to repeat the vote or correct the result. It does not cover votes on electing a prime minister or no-confidence votes.
The agreement takes effect at the next vote on Nov. 25 and runs on a trial basis until April 1, 2027.
stories.summary: All eight parties in the Riksdag agreed on a new pairing system that lets lawmakers miss votes without changing the balance of the chamber. The old arrangement collapsed in April during a vote on citizenship rules.

stories.headline: SJ to relaunch Stockholm-Berlin night train in December
more: Initially two trains a week will run to Berlin and one will stop in Hamburg; from Jan. 19 only one will continue to Berlin. Travelers from western Sweden can board in Lund.
The subsidy ended in September under the new Moderate-led government. SJ says fewer departures with a longer train make the route viable on its own.
stories.summary: Swedish rail operator SJ will restart its night train to Berlin on Dec. 13, running three departures a week in each direction without state subsidy.

briefs.text: Cal-Maine Foods, the largest U.S. egg producer, will cull about 1.8 million birds after bird flu was found at one of its Florida facilities.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and intelligence chief Jay Clayton faced questions in Congress on Wednesday about recent outages, flight disruptions and ICE tactics.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, valuing AI company at $1.5 trillion
more: The pricing points to strong investor demand for AI stocks despite worries about an AI bubble and market jitters after the ouster of Nvidia's CEO.

Anthropic is unprofitable under standard accounting rules and carries $6.2 billion in debt. It has committed about $900 billion to computing power and infrastructure, including $70 billion over the next 12 months.

The company is a public-benefit corporation, and a long-term benefit trust can elect or remove a majority of its board. Risks it faces include possible regulation from the incoming Democratic-led Congress and local opposition to data centers.
stories.summary: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above the expected range of $70 to $78, giving the artificial intelligence company a valuation of about $1.5 trillion. The sale of 980 million Class A shares raises about $81 billion, more than SpaceX's roughly $75 billion offering in June. Trading begins Thursday on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

stories.headline: House Democrats nominate Jeffries as first Black speaker nominee
more: The full House votes on the speaker when the new Congress is sworn in on Jan. 3, 2027.

Several incoming progressives who opposed him said he had not committed to policies including Medicare for All, stopping ICE, limiting money in politics and ending the war in Gaza. Former Speaker Nancy Pelosi congratulated him.
stories.summary: House Democrats on Wednesday formally nominated Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York for speaker in a closed-door caucus vote of 251 to 11, making him the first Black lawmaker formally nominated for the post. Democrats won control of both chambers in this month's midterm elections, and Jeffries is expected to succeed Republican Speaker Mike Johnson.

stories.headline: Record rain floods South Florida and collapses synagogue roof
more: Fort Lauderdale got 5.72 inches, breaking a daily record set in 1959. Hollywood declared a state of emergency, stretches of Interstate 95 and the Florida Turnpike were closed, and schools in Broward and Miami-Dade counties are closed Thursday.

Forecasters said up to 12 more inches of rain is possible along Florida's Atlantic coast through Friday, and a low near the northern Bahamas could become a subtropical or tropical storm early next week.
stories.summary: Heavy rain linked to El Nino flooded roads across South Florida, with parts of Broward County recording 15.3 inches in the 24 hours to Wednesday, according to preliminary National Weather Service figures. The roof of Temple Sinai in Hollywood collapsed, and no injuries were reported.

briefs.text: Russian strikes killed at least five people in Ukraine on Wednesday, four of them in Odesa, where officials said missiles hit the historic center.
An Iraqi court sentenced six French nationals to life in prison for joining ISIL, bringing the number convicted in the case to 16.

stories.headline: Iran widens Gulf attacks to U.S. air base in Kuwait
more: Washington described the Qeshm strike as retaliation for an Iranian attack on a U.S. radar site in Bahrain. Iran says its attacks respond to U.S. drone surveillance and a strike on Iranian communications towers. Kuwait's Foreign Ministry called the attacks criminal.

UAE oil company ADNOC said one tanker crew member was missing and 11 injured after an attack in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, where U.S. warships are escorting tankers under a naval blockade of Iran.
stories.summary: Iran targeted Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait and several U.S. facilities in Bahrain, including the base of the Navy's 5th Fleet, early Wednesday, a day after a U.S. jet struck a Revolutionary Guard missile site on Qeshm Island. Kuwait said its air defenses intercepted drones with no immediate damage, and Bahrain said it intercepted a number of attacks.

stories.headline: Israel launches first ground push in central Gaza since ceasefire
more: Hamas called the operation a flagrant violation of the ceasefire and said forced evacuations amount to a war crime. Israel's military said it reserves the right to act against immediate threats anywhere in Gaza.
Gaza's Health Ministry reported seven deaths and 15 wounded in the previous 24 hours.
stories.summary: Israeli tanks moved near Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps in central Gaza on Wednesday in what the army said was an operation to remove a threat to its forces near the Yellow Line set under the October 2025 ceasefire. Hospital officials said three Palestinians were killed in the operation, and families fled parts of Nuseirat.

stories.headline: Hegseth announces restored military partnership on surprise Caracas trip
more: Hegseth said the aim was to stabilize Venezuela and rid it of drug traffickers. U.S. forces seized former President Nicolas Maduro in January; Washington says he will be tried on weapons and drug charges. Critics say the U.S. is treating Venezuela as a vassal state.
Hegseth was due in Colombia later the same day.
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday and announced an agreement with Venezuela's interim government to resume military cooperation, including intelligence sharing and joint training. Interim President Delcy Rodriguez called it a resumption of the two countries' military relationship.

asl.hook: Your C hand is the cup; you are just taking a sip.
steps: Form your dominant hand into the letter C, as if holding a cup.
Bring the hand near your mouth.
Move it to your mouth in a short arc, tipping the imaginary cup.
For an alcoholic drink, change the C handshape to a Y.
For a shot or small cup, use a G handshape instead.
asl.tip: To show chugging, hold the sign longer while making a series of swallowing movements.

fact.text: Greenland sharks are the longest-lived vertebrates known: radiocarbon dating of their eye lenses suggests they live at least 272 years, and the largest animal studied was estimated at about 392 years old. They grow only about 1 cm a year and are thought to reach maturity at around 150.

lead.headline: Ukraine says it cut the road link on Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
more: Ukraine's General Staff said the rail line was still standing, though one arch was damaged; AP could not independently verify images released by Kyiv. Russia's Defense Ministry said it downed 1,441 Ukrainian drones overnight. No casualties were reported at the bridge, while Russian strikes killed at least two people in Kyiv and two in Zaporizhzhia.

The strikes came as Ukraine held online peace talks on Monday with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and officials from France, Germany, Britain, Italy and Poland. Kushner said progress was being made but difficult decisions remain. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Moscow has not agreed to widen talks to include Europe, and no date has been set for the next round.
lead.summary: Ukraine said a combined drone and missile strike overnight into Tuesday brought down an arch and a span of the road section of the Kerch Bridge, the only direct link between Russia and occupied Crimea. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the operation unprecedented and said it was the final stage of weeks of strikes on air defenses and radars around the bridge. Russia confirmed drone damage without details; the Kremlin said the bridge will be restored, and Crimea's Russian-installed governor said road traffic was halted while rail service resumed Tuesday afternoon. Russia struck two main bridges in Kyiv with ballistic missiles in the same period.

briefs.text: The Federal Council has proposed accepting a parliamentary motion for a fully digital, standardized process for cancelling health insurance, as only about 8 percent of policyholders switch providers each year.
Online shopping fraud is the most common form of cybercrime in Switzerland, according to a study by insurer Baloise Helvetia, which warned of higher risks around Black Friday and Christmas.
About 50 churches in eastern Switzerland report that bells no longer ring properly after this summer's heat dried out the wooden structures that hold them, public broadcaster RTS reported.
Chair Airlines plans daily flights from Zurich to Southend-on-Sea, about 35 miles from London, starting May 27.

stories.headline: Leak says Deutsche Bank ran Russian oligarchs' accounts from Zurich and Geneva
more: The documents, which reach back more than a decade, suggest Swiss banking secrecy made it hard to share client data within the group, and that customer checks were not applied as strictly as required. After Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the bank found a way in March 2022 to disclose at least some data to US authorities.
In a statement on Tuesday, Deutsche Bank said the incidents were old issues and that it is a different institution today.
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank managed assets for about 20 Russian oligarchs through its Swiss branches in Zurich and Geneva for years, the Tages-Anzeiger reported, based on millions of leaked internal documents also analyzed by Der Spiegel, Der Standard, The New York Times and the Financial Times. Some of the clients had close ties to Vladimir Putin that were known inside the bank, according to the reports.

stories.headline: Drought and heat cut Swiss farm incomes by 17 percent
more: Sugar beet yields fell by a third and potato yields by about a quarter, the lowest harvests for both in 30 years. Fodder crop yields dropped almost 20 percent, and falling pig prices added to the losses.
The decline follows a strong 2025, when average farm incomes rose 7.5 percent to 87,900 francs.
stories.summary: Net income in Swiss agriculture is expected to fall 17 percent this year to 2.8 billion francs after a hot, dry summer, the Federal Statistical Office said on Tuesday. Gross value added is estimated to drop 11.7 percent to 4.5 billion francs.

stories.headline: Petition with 100,000 signatures opposes new hurdle for psychotherapy
more: The petition is backed by three professional associations of psychologists and psychotherapists. They argue an extra psychiatrist appointment would tie up scarce capacity and hit children, young people and rural residents hardest.

Since mid-2022, psychological psychotherapists have been able to bill basic health insurance directly on a doctor's referral. Billed costs rose sharply after the change before slowing, according to the Swiss Health Observatory.
stories.summary: A petition with more than 100,000 signatures was submitted in Bern on Tuesday opposing a plan that would require patients to get a psychiatrist's diagnosis before starting psychological psychotherapy. A committee of the National Council has proposed the change to curb costs and focus care on people with severe conditions.

Seventy percent of immigrants aged 15 to 64 were employed in 2025, up 13 points from 2005 but below the 81 percent rate for people without an immigrant background, the Federal Statistical Office said.
Thuringia's domestic intelligence office reported a surge in membership of far-right extremist groups last year, with about 400 people classed as violence-prone.
Germany beat the Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin on Monday to reach the Nations League quarterfinals, with Florian Wirtz scoring twice.

stories.headline: German coalition leaders reach deal after overnight talks on electricity tax
more: Financing was the main sticking point before the meeting. According to dpa-AFX, the conservatives proposed using surpluses in the renewable energy account, which the SPD considers constitutionally risky, while the SPD floated higher corporate or capital gains taxes. Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil's ministry said it wanted no financial experiments.

The coalition needs to close a gap of roughly 7 billion euros in the 2027 budget. Merz promised the tax cut after his party's heavy election losses in mid-October. Comparison site Verivox estimated a three-person household would save about 7.75 euros a month.
stories.summary: Leaders of Germany's governing CDU, CSU and SPD reached an agreement early Wednesday after roughly eight hours of talks in which a cut to the electricity tax took up much of the time, party sources said. Details had not been released and were to be presented first to the parliamentary groups and then in a written statement on Wednesday morning, with no news conference planned. Chancellor Friedrich Merz had sought to lower the tax to the EU minimum for all consumers from January 1, 2027, a step estimated to cost about 5.4 billion euros a year. Pension reform, a fuel price cap and electoral law were also on the agenda.

stories.headline: Tesla to invest 3 billion euros to build robotaxis near Berlin
more: The plant, Tesla's only factory in Europe, employs about 11,000 people, and the company says it is hiring hundreds more. Brandenburg state premier Dietmar Woidke called the decision economically very significant, and IG Metall's regional leader called it good news, though the union has accused Tesla of poor working conditions.
The announcement contrasts with cutbacks elsewhere in the German car industry: Volkswagen is cutting tens of thousands of jobs and Mercedes said last week it would halt investment in Germany.
stories.summary: Tesla said it will invest 3 billion euros to expand its factory in Gruenheide outside Berlin, with a new facility eventually able to produce up to one million driverless Cybercabs a year. Construction is due to start in the first half of 2027, with production planned for 2029.

stories.headline: Ifo study says big power firms inflated prices in energy crisis
more: From September 2021, actual market prices ran about 45 euros per megawatt-hour above a simulated competitive price, and about 20 euros above it under the most conservative assumptions. RWE, LEAG, EnBW, Uniper and Vattenfall hold about 56 percent of conventional plant capacity.
Ifo warned the trend is worsening, noting that RWE and LEAG won 94 percent of the subsidized capacity in the first tender for new gas-fired plants.
stories.summary: Germany's five largest electricity producers used their market power to push up prices during the 2021-22 energy crisis, earning an estimated 10.7 to 20.5 billion euros in extra revenue, according to a study by the Ifo Institute. The researchers said the price spikes could not be explained by higher generation costs alone.

stories.headline: Life satisfaction in Germany falls for first time since 2021
more: Declines were sharper among women, adults aged 18 to 39, students, the unemployed and single parents, and satisfaction with personal finances fell for a second year.
Bavaria ranked highest. Berlin scored 6.79, ahead of only Saarland and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
stories.summary: Average life satisfaction in Germany fell 0.09 points to 7.00 on a scale of zero to 10, the first decline since 2021, according to the annual SKL Happiness Atlas based on surveys of more than 12,000 people. The share of highly satisfied people dropped from 48 to 44 percent.

briefs.text: A single dose of CAR-T cell therapy brought substantial improvement to people with stiff person syndrome, a rare autoimmune disorder, in an early three-site trial published in JAMA Neurology; some patients returned to work and walking, though researchers say larger studies are needed.

A coyote became the first large mammal photographed using the Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing over 10 lanes of the 101 Freeway near Los Angeles, weeks before the bridge's official opening on Dec. 2.

Oregon State University chemists reported a metal-organic framework that keeps capturing carbon dioxide from humid exhaust by holding water and CO2 in separate parts of its pores, working over dozens of cycles in lab tests (Angewandte Chemie).

stories.headline: First sea turtle hatchlings from natural West Coast nests reach the Pacific
more: The eggs were cared for by the aquarium with state and federal wildlife authorities, and a third nest was documented in Ventura County on Nov. 1. The aquarium did not give the number of hatchlings released.
Scientists do not yet know why the turtles chose Southern California beaches; the aquarium said it may signal a historic shift with long-term implications for the species.
stories.summary: Olive ridley sea turtle hatchlings from two Southern California nests were released into the Pacific before dawn on Nov. 14 and 15, the Aquarium of the Pacific said. The nests, found in mid-September at Seal Beach and Huntington Beach, are the first confirmed natural sea turtle nesting on the U.S. West Coast. The aquarium said all of the hatchlings made it from the sand to the sea.

briefs.text: Money markets put the chance of a Riksbank rate hike in December at 36 percent, up from 16 percent a week earlier, according to SEB; the next decision is on December 16.
Princess Estelle is spending part of her school work placement at the Swedish embassy in Helsinki and the office of Finnish President Alexander Stubb.

stories.headline: Speaker pauses Swedish government talks for a week, sets Christmas goal
more: Norlen will consult all party leaders next Tuesday or Wednesday. A vote on a prime minister could follow in late November, with priority for any party that presents a workable government, SVT reported.

The center-left parties led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson are expected to open talks this week, TT reported, but the Left Party still wants cabinet posts, which the Centre Party rejects. Under Swedish rules, four failed votes trigger a new election.
stories.summary: Speaker Andreas Norlen granted a one-week pause in government formation on Tuesday after caretaker Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said he had been unable to form a center-right government and asked for more time. Norlen said Swedes will know by Christmas whether they get a new government or a snap election.

stories.headline: Prosecutor seeks record fine for LKAB over Kiruna diesel leak
more: The full scale of the leak only became clear when the tank was shut down, and clean-up is still under way. Prosecutor Christer B Jarlas said the county board's late report in 2025 complicated the investigation and could affect issues such as the statute of limitations.
stories.summary: A prosecutor is seeking a corporate fine of at least 180 million kronor against mining company LKAB after two million liters of diesel leaked from a storage tank at its Kiruna site over nine months in 2021. If granted, it would be the largest corporate fine ever imposed in Sweden.

briefs.text: Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader in a secret-ballot vote set for Dec. 1; Schumer says he has the votes to stay.
Online services at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and other banks recovered early Tuesday after Monday outages; Chase blamed a software bug that affected transactions with other banks.

stories.headline: U.S. loses measles elimination status for first time since 2000
more: Cases have been confirmed in 45 states and the District of Columbia, with more than 590 hospitalizations and at least six deaths. Pennsylvania has reported more than 1,500 cases. CDC data show 96 percent of this year's patients were unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status.

Regaining the status requires vaccination rates of 95 percent or more, strong surveillance and fast outbreak response verified by PAHO. Sen. Bill Cassidy said Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and other officials should do more to promote vaccination.
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization said Tuesday that the United States no longer counts as having eliminated measles, after the virus spread continuously for at least 12 months. Mexico also lost its status. The CDC has counted 5,412 U.S. cases so far in 2026, more than double last year's total.

stories.headline: Nvidia beats forecasts as board rules out Huang's return
more: The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $127.4 billion to $132.6 billion. Chief financial officer Colette Kress remains interim CEO, and the board said it has hired search firms and will consider internal and external candidates.

Huang resigned after disclosures about his personal conduct and said he would cooperate with the board's independent investigation. A petition calling for his reinstatement has drawn more than 190,000 signatures.
stories.summary: Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion on Tuesday, up 103 percent from a year earlier and above analyst estimates, in its first report since chief executive Jensen Huang resigned. Board chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Huang, hours after Huang said he would be honored to return. Shares rose about 3.6 percent in overnight trading.

stories.headline: Administration details $50 billion request to overhaul air traffic system
more: Friday's ground stop led to thousands of canceled flights, and the FAA has stopped installing routers it linked to the disruption. Lawmakers' response to the request was not yet clear.

A string of other outages followed: the NSA's classified internal network went down on Tuesday, which two officials attributed to routine patching rather than a cyberattack, and customers of several major banks had trouble reaching accounts on Monday.
stories.summary: The Trump administration sent lawmakers an updated request for about $50.1 billion to modernize U.S. aviation, days after outdated equipment triggered a rare nationwide ground stop. The plan splits roughly $10 billion each among air traffic control upgrades, airport infrastructure, terminals at major hubs, five new control centers and up to 140 FAA towers.

briefs.text: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Brexit's promises were not kept and plans to open talks on a closer long-term relationship with the EU after a Brussels summit on Friday.
A Dublin court sentenced Riad Bouchaker to life in prison for the attempted murder of three children in the November 2023 knife attack outside a school that set off the city's worst riots in decades.

stories.headline: Iran targets U.S. radar in Bahrain again as tankers are hit near Hormuz
more: Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said a regional bloc backed an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under an initial ceasefire, which the bloc's members did not confirm. The Trump administration has rejected Iran's demands for sanctions relief and an end to the naval blockade.

Iran said it will not admit U.N. nuclear inspectors to damaged sites until the war has permanently ended. The USS Theodore Roosevelt joined two other U.S. carriers in the region. Brent crude traded near $95 a barrel, compared with about $72 before the war began Feb. 28.
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Tuesday it targeted a U.S. radar at Isa Air Base in Bahrain, its third such claim since Friday, citing U.S. drone flights over Iran. Bahrain said its air defenses intercepted the drones, and no casualties were reported. Separately, Iran's navy said a tanker struck a mine and caught fire, and a British maritime agency reported another tanker disabled off Oman.

stories.headline: Trump signs Thailand trade statement in Manila before China talks
more: In China, Trump is scheduled to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen and three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Protesters in Manila carried signs opposing his visit and a planned U.S.-backed AI hub that critics say would displace farmers and Indigenous Aeta communities.

Also in Shenzhen, Xi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney agreed to widen tariff relief: China will ease duties on about 400 million Canadian dollars of pork, fish and seafood, and Canada extended exemptions on some Chinese steel and aluminum by two years.
stories.summary: President Trump opened his Asia trip in Manila on Tuesday, meeting leaders of the Quad for the first time since returning to office and signing a trade statement under which Thailand would cut tariffs on most U.S. goods and buy $2.6 billion in U.S. farm products. He is due to be welcomed by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday before flying to China.

stories.headline: Houthis advance in southwest Yemen as government forces pull back toward Aden
more: Houthi authorities said Saudi strikes killed or wounded 37 people in 24 hours. Saudi Arabia, which this week dismissed the commander of the coalition forces fighting the Houthis, has not commented.
stories.summary: Houthi rebels have pushed forward in Yemen's southwest, cutting a key government supply route along the Red Sea coast and forcing government troops to withdraw from positions near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend Aden, the temporary capital. Yemen's army said it carried out 661 attacks on Houthi positions and killed or wounded 173 fighters; the claims could not be independently verified.

asl.hook: You are pretending to pop a bite of food into your mouth.
asl.meaning: To eat; the related sign FOOD uses the same hand and location
steps: Make a flattened O hand: press your fingertips together against your thumb.
Bring the hand to your mouth.
Move it toward your mouth once, as if putting a bite of food in.
Keep your mouth closed while you sign.
For FOOD, Lifeprint notes the motion is often doubled; for ongoing eating, repeat the movement.
asl.tip: Use two hands for a group eating or a lot of eating; alternating two hands means pig out.

Built by the Suez Canal Company under a concession won by French diplomat Ferdinand de Lesseps, it took 10 years after work began in 1859, far longer than the six originally planned. It let ships sail between Europe and Asia without going around Africa.
